findings.issue_text: totalPages in admin-group.js.es6 is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100/50 yields 3 pages instead of 2); should be Math.ceil(user_count / limit)

In group_member.hbs, inside the group-member itemView the template context is the member, so {{#unless automatic}} resolves against the user object (always falsy) rather than the group; the remove icon is rendered for automatic groups and clicking it gets a 422 from the server

In groups_controller.rb remove_member, group.users.delete(user_id) removes the join record directly without updating the in-memory user_count; the subsequent group.save persists the stale count, leaving groups.user_count out of sync
In groups_controller.rb update, group.visible = params[:visible] == "true" is unconditional; API clients that omit visible (previously tolerated) will silently flip the group to invisible

In groups_controller.rb members, limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i has no upper cap, allowing limit=1000000 to serialize every group member in one request (DoS/data-dumping vector); negative limit/offset also produce invalid SQL LIMIT/OFFSET and a 500

In groups_controller.rb add_members, usernames.split(",") doesn't strip whitespace, so "bob, alice" silently fails to add alice; non-existent usernames are skipped with no error, returning success even when nothing was added

The public group page (members.hbs / group-members.js.es6) now renders only the first 50 members (limit default changed) and no pagination UI was added, so members beyond the first page are unreachable — feature regression

Breaking API changes without deprecation in config/routes.rb:49: GET /admin/groups/:id/users is removed and GET /groups/:name/members response shape changed from a bare array to {members, meta}, breaking third-party consumers
In admin-group.js.es6 addMembers, the user-selector input is never cleared after adding, so clicking "Add" twice re-adds the same users

In group.js findMembers, rapid next/previous clicks fire overlapping AJAX requests; responses can resolve out of order and setProperties renders a stale page (no request cancellation or sequence guard, and offset is optimistic before server confirmation)

Test gap in admin/groups_controller_spec.rb remove_member: the "cannot remove members" test uses xhr :put while the route is DELETE, so the real verb/routing is never exercised; there are also no specs for the new pagination/meta behavior of groups#members

In group.hbs, buttons inside <form class="form-horizontal"> lack type="button", so pressing Enter in the name field natively submits the form (full page reload) instead of running the Ember save action

goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

In groups_controller.rb update, group.visible = params[:visible] == "true" is unconditional; API clients that omit visible (previously tolerated) will silently flip the group to invisible

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#update the line `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` runs regardless of whether `params[:visible]` was provided. If a client omits `visible`, `params[:visible]` is nil and the expression evaluates to false, so the group can be unintentionally set to invisible. This is a correctness issue visible in the diff (though similar unconditional behavior also existed previously when using `payload[:visible]`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: In groups_controller.rb members, limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i has no upper cap, allowing limit=1000000 to serialize every group member in one request (DoS/data-dumping vector); negative limit/offset also produce invalid SQL LIMIT/OFFSET and a 500

adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members, the new pagination logic takes `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and passes them directly into `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no validation or upper bound. This makes it verifiable that a client can request an arbitrarily large limit (e.g., 1000000) causing the server to load/serialize a huge number of users in one response. Also, because there is no guard against negative values, `limit` or `offset` can become negative (e.g., `?limit=-5&offset=-10`), which can produce invalid SQL (Postgres rejects negative LIMIT/OFFSET) and thus a 500 error path. The issue is present in the diff and is not merely stylistic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In groups_controller.rb add_members, usernames.split(",") doesn't strip whitespace, so "bob, alice" silently fails to add alice; non-existent usernames are skipped with no error, returning success even when nothing was added

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, `usernames` is taken as a raw string and iterated via `usernames.split(",")`. The loop passes each token directly to `User.find_by_username(username)` without `strip`, so an input like "bob, alice" yields a second token " alice" which will not match a username "alice" and will be silently skipped. Additionally, any non-existent usernames are skipped due to the `if user = ...` guard, and the action still proceeds to `group.save` and renders `success_json` on success, so the request can return success even if no users were actually added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The public group page (members.hbs / group-members.js.es6) now renders only the first 50 members (limit default changed) and no pagination UI was added, so members beyond the first page are unreachable — feature regression

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always apply pagination with a default `limit` of 50 and returns only that slice (`limit/offset`). On the client, `Discourse.Group#findMembers` now requests `/groups/:name/members.json` with `limit`/`offset` and sets `members` on the model, but the public `group-members` route/template (`group-members.js.es6` + `group/members.hbs`) only calls `model.findMembers()` once and adds no pagination controls/actions (unlike the admin UI which adds next/previous). Therefore the public members page will render only the first page (50) and provides no way in this diff to load subsequent pages, making members beyond the first 50 effectively unreachable via the UI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Breaking API changes without deprecation in config/routes.rb:49: GET /admin/groups/:id/users is removed and GET /groups/:name/members response shape changed from a bare array to {members, meta}, breaking third-party consumers

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes two concrete, backward-incompatible interface changes. (1) In config/routes.rb, the nested route under admin/groups removes `get "users"` and replaces it with `delete "members"` and `put "members"`, so any client calling the previous GET endpoint will break. (2) In GroupsController#members, the response changes from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (a bare serialized list) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: ... }`, which changes the JSON shape for `/groups/:name/members(.json)` and will break consumers expecting an array payload.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In admin-group.js.es6 addMembers, the user-selector input is never cleared after adding, so clicking "Add" twice re-adds the same users

adjudication.rationale: The `addMembers` action in `admin-group.js.es6` calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"))` but never resets `usernames` afterward. Since the `user-selector` in `group.hbs` is bound to `usernames`, the input will retain the previous value, so clicking "Add" again will submit the same usernames again (at minimum causing a repeated request / re-attempt to add the same members). The inline comment `// TODO: should clear the input` also corroborates this missing behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In group.hbs, buttons inside <form class="form-horizontal"> lack type="button", so pressing Enter in the name field natively submits the form (full page reload) instead of running the Ember save action

adjudication.rationale: The updated `group.hbs` wraps the controls in `<form class="form-horizontal">` and uses plain `<button {{action "save"}} ...>` (also the add and destroy buttons) without an explicit `type`. In HTML, a `<button>` inside a form defaults to `type="submit"`. There is no `{{action}}` bound to the form’s submit event, so pressing Enter in the name text field can trigger a native form submit, which is not prevented by the button’s click handler and can cause a full page navigation/reload instead of just running the Ember action.
